subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance
message_1_subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance
message_1_body:
Alex —

Thanks again for the 30-minute call today. Quick recap of what we discussed and the proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Pain points / goals:
- Current LLM endpoints are inconsistent during marketing spikes: observed latency p95 up to ~1.2s and periodic failures when concurrency spikes.
- Cost unpredictability from on-demand GPU usage — finance needs a more predictable monthly spend for forecasting.
- Data isolation requirement for certain customer cohorts (financial data) — must run in a dedicated environment with audit logs.

Current stack / usage signals you shared:
- Production use: customer support summarization + compliant PII redaction.
- Typical steady-state: ~40 QPS; peak (campaigns): ~130 QPS for ~2-3 hours.
- Average response size: ~120 tokens; typical prompt length: 30–50 tokens.
- Daily token volume (approx): 18–25M tokens.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Predictable monthly spend (prefer committed monthly) and clear burst pricing.
- P95 latency target: <= 400ms for typical support prompts.
- Isolation for regulated cohorts (separate tenant/dedicated GPU pool, retention controls, KMS integration).
- Ability to autoscale within predictable bounds and burst to handle 2x peak for short windows.

Dedicated capacity fit (initial sizing notes):
- Based on the numbers above and our throughput models, a small dedicated pool (2 x A100-equivalent) with autoscale-to-4 for bursts would cover steady-state + 2x peak headroom for short windows, with expected p95 latency in the 250–400ms range depending on prompt mix and quantization.
- Billing: reserved monthly commit for baseline capacity + metered burst usage. We’ll include the proposed pricing options in the follow-up.

Open questions / asks from Aurora:
- Can you share a 24h traffic histogram (CSV or logs) so we can refine the sizing?
- Any hard constraints on retention/audit windows or KMS providers to support the dedicated/private deployment?
- Preferred contract start date / procurement timeline?

Next steps (we recommend):
1) I’ll circulate a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and an initial sizing/pricing estimate by EOD Tuesday.
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) to go over prompt samples, latency SLOs, and network/security requirements.
3) You share a sample traffic histogram and a representative prompt set (anonymized) so we can run a quick perf simulation.

I’ve attached a draft MAP and an SLA outline to get the ball rolling. Marissa will follow up to propose times for the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment stubs: Aurora-MAP-draft.pdf (MAP), Dedicated-SLA-draft.docx (SLA outline)
message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance
message_2_body:
Thanks, Rafael — really helpful summary and aligns with what we need. Quick clarifications: 

- Peak QPS: our observability shows a sustained 90–120 QPS during recent campaigns; the 130 QPS number was a 10–15 minute burst. Planning for autoscale-to-2x peak (so ~250 QPS) is reasonable.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms is our target; 99th should ideally be < 600ms.
- Billing/contract: Finance prefers a predictable committed baseline with a clear per-minute burst rate rather than pure metered. Can your proposal include a committed baseline + capped burst billing option?
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and our legal team will want the KMS/HSM integration details. I’ll attach a short security questionnaire — can Marissa or your security contact take point?

We’ll share a 24-hour traffic histogram and anonymized prompt set (CSV) by Monday. Procurement timeline: aim to have an approved vendor decision by end of next month if the numbers line up.

Happy to jump on the technical deep-dive — Tuesday or Wednesday next week works.

—
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, Aurora Finance
alex.johnson@aurorafinance.com | +1 (650) 555-0189
